name: Pondu
subtitle: Pondu is the Congolese name for cassava leaves and for the dish made from them.

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: Cassava leaves, described as an emblematic dish of the DR Congo.

facts.label: How it is made
facts.value: Whole leaves are first turned into ground leaves, which are then cooked into the prepared pondu dish.

facts.label: Cooking time
facts.value: Cooking cassava leaves (pondu or pondu-madesu) takes at least 120 minutes.

facts.label: Versions
facts.value: The most common are pondu ya madesu (with beans), limbondo (with bicarbonate) and saka saka or matamba (without bicarbonate or beans).

facts.label: Quantity eaten
facts.value: Households and hotels, restaurants and cafés in Kinshasa consume about 699,685 tonnes of cassava leaves a year (Kinkela et al., 2017).

facts.label: Cultural value
facts.value: A household survey found that cassava leaves and chikwangue have strong symbolic and cultural value.

facts.label: Daily food
facts.value: Cassava leaves are part of the daily meals of Kinshasa residents.

facts.label: Markets
facts.value: Commonly called pondu, cassava leaves are the most visible produce on Kinshasa's market stalls.

parts.text: Pondu is the Congolese name for cassava leaves and for the dish made from them. The leaves are first ground and then cooked into the prepared dish, for at least two hours. The most common versions in Kinshasa are pondu ya madesu (with beans), limbondo (with bicarbonate) and saka saka or matamba (with neither).
Cassava leaves are part of the daily meals of Kinshasa residents and the most visible produce on the city's market stalls.
